grades.quote: The CSRRS[I] an CSRRC[I] instructions only action side effects for fields for which the _rs1_ or _uimm_ argument has at least one bit set corresponding to that field.
grades.reason: Table 7 shows CSRRS/CSRRC with rs1 = x0 read but do not write the CSR, and with rs1 not x0 they both read and write. It also says CSRRS[I]/CSRRC[I] only action per-field side effects when the rs1 or uimm argument has set bits. It does not explicitly contrast x0 with a non-x0 register holding zero, and it mostly covers the immediate forms.
This is a vector strcmp code example. It uses csrr to read vl and says nothing about how CSRRS treats x0 compared with a register holding zero.

grades.quote: For both CSRRS and CSRRC, if _rs1_ = `x0` , then the instruction will not write to the CSR at all, and so shall not cause any of the side effects that might otherwise occur on a CSR write, nor raise illegalinstruction exceptions on accesses to read-only CSRs.
grades.reason: This passage answers the question directly. With rs1 = x0, CSRRS does not write the CSR, so it causes no write side effects and raises no illegal-instruction exception on read-only CSRs. With a non-x0 register holding zero, the instruction still writes the CSR. It does not action per-field side effects, but it does action side effects from writing the entire CSR.
